source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024)

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: About two-thirds of total body water is found in the:
questions.rationale: ICF holds about 2/3 of body water; ECF (interstitial, plasma, transcellular) holds about 1/3.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 14 Body fluid compartments (PDF p. 461)
questions.quote: It comprises 2/3 (70%) ofthe body fluid.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Why do women have a lower percentage of body water than men?
questions.rationale: Muscle holds water while fat does not; men are about 60% water, women about 50%, infants about 80%.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 14 Body water (PDF p. 461)
questions.quote: Females have more adipose tissues than males. Fats do not store water.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which hormone causes the kidneys to retain sodium and excrete potassium?
questions.rationale: Aldosterone is "pro-sodium, anti-potassium"; excess causes hypokalemia, deficiency (Addison's) hyperkalemia.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 14 Potassium regulation (PDF p. 462)
questions.quote: Aldosterone retains sodium and excretes potassium.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: The most reliable indicator of a client's fluid loss over 24 hours is:
questions.rationale: Weight change is the most objective indicator of fluid deficit or excess; urine output comes next.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 14 Dehydration (PDF p. 463)
questions.quote: The most objective indicator of dehydration is weight loss, next is decreased urine output.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which laboratory finding is expected in a dehydrated client?
questions.rationale: Water loss concentrates the blood: hematocrit, BUN and electrolytes rise; urine is concentrated.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 14 Dehydration (PDF p. 463)
questions.quote: Increased hematocrit (hemoconcentration), BUN, serum electrolyte levels.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A child given repeated tap-water enemas becomes confused and has a seizure. The most likely cause is:
questions.rationale: Electrolyte-free water shifts into cells; brain swelling raises ICP and causes confusion and seizures.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 14 Water intoxication (PDF p. 463)
questions.quote: The most dangerous effect of water intoxication is increased ICP.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Edema after an axillary node dissection for breast cancer is due to:
questions.rationale: Removal of lymph nodes blocks lymph drainage, so fluid collects in the tissues (lymphedema).
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 14 Edema (PDF p. 464)
questions.quote: Lymphatic obstruction, e.g. removal of lymph nodes in mastectomy

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client with liver cirrhosis has ascites and low serum albumin. The edema is mainly due to:
questions.rationale: Albumin holds fluid in vessels; hypoalbuminemia lowers oncotic pressure and fluid leaks out.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 14 Edema (PDF p. 464)
questions.quote: Decreased colloidal osmotic pressure (C.O.P.) or oncotic pressure (O.P.), e.g., hypoalbuminemia.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client on furosemide has a serum sodium of 124 mEq/L, headache and confusion. The nurse's priority is:
questions.rationale: Hyponatremia makes cells swell and can cause seizures; promote safety and give sodium as prescribed.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 14 Hyponatremia (PDF p. 465)
questions.quote: Safety precautions, e.g., use of side rails, supervision of ambulation.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: An elderly client with high fever has extreme thirst, a dry sticky tongue and restlessness. Sodium is 152 mEq/L. This is:
questions.rationale: Hypernatremia draws water out of cells: intense thirst, sticky membranes, restlessness and disorientation.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 14 Hypernatremia (PDF p. 466)
questions.quote: Extreme thirst Dry, sticky mucous membrane

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client on furosemide has muscle weakness, abdominal distention and weak reflexes. Which electrolyte is likely low?
questions.rationale: In hypokalemia "everything is low and slow": weakness, ileus, diminished reflexes, dysrhythmias.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 14 Hypokalemia (PDF p. 466)
questions.quote: In hypokalemia, "Everything is low and slow.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Before adding potassium chloride to an IV infusion, the nurse must first check:
questions.rationale: Potassium is excreted by the kidneys; confirm adequate urine output (at least 30 mL/hour) before giving it.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 14 Potassium replacement (PDF p. 475)
questions.quote: Ensure that urine output is adequate, 30 50 mls/hour before administering potassium.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: An order reads "KCl 20 mEq IV push now." The nurse should:
options: Withhold it and clarify the order
Dilute it in 5 mL and push
questions.rationale: Potassium chloride is never given IV push; it can cause fatal dysrhythmias. It is diluted and infused slowly.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 14 Hypokalemia (PDF p. 467)
questions.quote: NEVER administer Potassium Chloride per IV push or direct IV.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which ECG change is typical of hyperkalemia?
questions.rationale: Hyperkalemia causes peaked T waves, widened QRS and flat P waves; hypokalemia causes U waves and flat T.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 14 ECG changes (PDF p. 472)
questions.quote: Tall peaked T waves

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client in kidney failure has a potassium of 6.8 mEq/L and ECG changes. Which drug is given first to protect the heart?
questions.rationale: IV calcium stabilizes the myocardium; insulin with dextrose, resins and dialysis then lower potassium.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 14 Hyperkalemia (PDF p. 468)
questions.quote: Calcium gluconate per IV as prescribed. This is the antidote of hyperkalemia.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Regular insulin with dextrose is given for hyperkalemia because insulin:
questions.rationale: Insulin shifts potassium into cells, quickly lowering serum levels; dextrose prevents hypoglycemia.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 14 Hyperkalemia (PDF p. 468)
questions.quote: Dextrose 10% in water with regular insulin per IV as prescribed.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: After a thyroidectomy, the nurse inflates a BP cuff and the client's hand goes into spasm. This is:
questions.rationale: Carpal spasm with a BP cuff is Trousseau's sign; facial twitching on tapping is Chvostek's. Both indicate low calcium.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 14 Hypocalcemia (PDF p. 468)
questions.quote: Muscles: muscle spasm, tetany (Chvostek's sign and Trousseau's sign).

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A trauma client received many units of citrated blood. The nurse watches for:
questions.rationale: Citrate binds ionized calcium, so massive transfusion can cause hypocalcemia (tingling, tetany).
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 14 Hypocalcemia (PDF p. 468)
questions.quote: large blood transfusion with citrated blood

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A bedridden client with bone metastases has constipation, lethargy and weak reflexes. Calcium is high. The nurse encourages:
questions.rationale: Hypercalcemia: increase fluids to prevent dehydration and kidney stones; mobilize and avoid calcium sources.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 14 Hypercalcemia (PDF p. 470)
questions.quote: Increase fluid intake (3 to 4 L/day). To prevent dehydration due to polyuria and to prevent renal stone formation.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client with chronic alcoholism has tremors, hyperactive reflexes and tetany. Which electrolyte is likely low?
questions.rationale: Hypomagnesemia (from malnutrition, alcohol withdrawal) increases acetylcholine release: tremors, tetany, seizures.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 14 Hypomagnesemia (PDF p. 470)
questions.quote: prolonged malnutrition or starvation; malabsorption syndromes, hypercalcemia, alcohol withdrawal syndromes

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client with renal failure using magnesium antacids has drowsiness, low BP and absent deep tendon reflexes. The nurse suspects:
questions.rationale: Excess magnesium depresses neuromuscular activity; calcium gluconate is the antagonist.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 14 Hypermagnesemia (PDF p. 471)
questions.quote: Diminished or loss of deep tendon reflexes.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client on digoxin is most at risk for toxicity if which lab value is present?
questions.rationale: Hypokalemia, hypomagnesemia and hypercalcemia all increase the risk of digitalis toxicity.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 14 Electrolyte replacement (PDF p. 475)
questions.quote: Hypomagnesemia + Digoxin = Digitalis Toxicity

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client oversedated with morphine has a respiratory rate of 6. The ABG will most likely show:
questions.rationale: Hypoventilation retains CO2, lowering pH: respiratory acidosis.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 14 Respiratory acidosis (PDF p. 472)
questions.quote: Disorders that lead to hypoventilation result to retention of carbon dioxide.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: An anxious student breathing fast before her board exam reports tingling fingers and lightheadedness. This suggests:
questions.rationale: Hyperventilation blows off CO2 and causes respiratory alkalosis; coach slow breathing and treat the cause.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 14 Respiratory alkalosis (PDF p. 473)
questions.quote: lightheadedness; numbness, tingling of fingers and toes, tetany

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client in diabetic ketoacidosis has deep, rapid breathing. This breathing pattern is an attempt to:
options: Blow off CO2 to raise pH
questions.rationale: Kussmaul breathing compensates for metabolic acidosis by exhaling CO2.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 14 Metabolic acidosis (PDF p. 473)
questions.quote: Kussmaul's breathing (deep, rapid breathing which is an attempt to blow ofTC02)

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client with an NG tube on continuous suction for 3 days is at risk for:
questions.rationale: Loss of gastric acid (vomiting, suction, lavage) causes metabolic alkalosis with hypokalemia.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 14 Metabolic alkalosis (PDF p. 474)
questions.quote: vomiting, gastric suctioning, intestinal fistulas.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Acidosis is commonly accompanied by which potassium change?
questions.rationale: In acidosis, potassium shifts out of cells and its excretion falls (hyperkalemia); alkalosis causes hypokalemia.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 14 Potassium regulation (PDF p. 462)
questions.quote: (Alkalosis: hypokalemia; Acidosis: hyperkalemia)

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client drank 10 oz of soup, 8 oz of water and 4 oz of juice. What is the intake to record?
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 14 Critical thinking answers (PDF p. 481)
questions.quote: One oz. is equivalent to 30 ml.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client on TPN has a blood glucose of 260 mg/dL. Which may be the cause?
questions.rationale: TPN is hypertonic dextrose; too rapid an infusion causes hyperglycemia. Insulin may be added as ordered.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 14 Nutritional support (PDF p. 476)
questions.quote: Hyperglycemia may also occur when infusion rate for TPN is too rapid.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: The most common complication of TPN is:
questions.rationale: Infection is the most common complication; use strict asepsis and change the solution and tubing as scheduled.
questions.source: Udan, Comprehensive Nursing Licensure Review Vol. 2 (2024), Ch. 14 Nutritional support (PDF p. 476)
questions.quote: The most common complication of TPN infusion is infection, especially at the insertion site of TPN catheter.
